report_title: Ad smoke test: memberships and class packs add-on for fitness studios

plan.decision: If at least one promise clears the pass line at Meta's real cost, build the add-on and lead its launch with that promise; if none clears the kill line, don't build it on this pitch.

economics.formula: allowed cost per sign-up = allowed cost per customer x sign-up-to-customer rate = $150 x 0.20

left_out.reason: category term: searchers want a whole studio system, not an add-on
asks for a no-cost tool; won't pay $29

channels.land_rate_source: default 85%; no Search history for this offer
channels.why: The test set gets 530 searches a month, about 247.3 in 14 days. Even if one search in ten clicked, that is 24.7 clicks against 209 needed.

channels.source: facebook-ads search_interests, estimate_audience_size, get_minimum_budgets, get_insights_adaccount; google-analytics get_report
channels.audience: US, 25 to 60, Pilates or Yoga studio interest, and Small business owners
channels.land_rate_source: GA4 facebook / paid sessions 2,217 / 2,704 link clicks
channels.why: Fits the $2,000 cap at $1,601.47, the audience is large enough (0.27 planned impressions per person), and studio owners are found by who they are, not by what they search.

channels.cpc_source: suggested bid (default) for the owner job titles
channels.why: Each visit costs $13.41, so 44.7% of visitors would have to sign up to stay under $30.00 a sign-up. Cold paid traffic doesn't do that; above 25% the skill won't plan a test.
No Reddit Ads costs were pasted. Paste a CPC from a past Reddit campaign to include it.

sizing.pass_line_formula: cost per visit $1.73 / allowed cost per sign-up $30.00
sizing.visits_formula: one-sided 95% confidence, 80% power, kill line against pass line
sizing.budget_formula: 804 visits x $1.73 x 1.15 buffer for cost drift
sizing.detectable_gap_note: With 268 visits each, two promises must differ by about 6.2 points before the test can call one better (alpha 0.025 per comparison). Smaller gaps read as not proven.

setup: One Meta campaign, traffic objective optimised for landing page views, three ad sets with their own budgets (no campaign budget).
Same audience, placements, image and call to action in every ad set; only the headline and first line change.
Each ad links to the same page with its own ?v= and utm_content, and the page shows the matching headline.
Sign-ups are counted by the GA4 key event waitlist_signup, not by Meta's lead count.
Before launch, submit one test sign-up on each page version and confirm it reaches GA4.

honest_note.thank_you_page: Thanks for joining. Memberships and class packs aren't available yet: we're deciding what to build first and you're helping. We'll email you once, when it opens or if we decide not to build it. No payment is taken.
honest_note.ad_copy_rule: Ads say 'coming soon' or 'join the waitlist'; none says 'start today' or implies it can be bought now.
honest_note.follow_up: Email every sign-up with the outcome by 2026-11-20, whichever way the decision goes.

frozen_rule: Read each promise only after it reaches 268 visits, or when the $1,601.47 budget is spent.
Go: sign-up rate at or above 5.77% and actual cost per sign-up at or under $30.00.
Real but short: rate at or above the critical rate for its visit count, but not a go.
Stop: rate under the critical rate (the test can't tell it apart from the kill line).
A promise is 'proven better' than another only if a two-proportion test gives p under 0.025.
No early stop for good news. Early stop only if tracking breaks or spend reaches the cap.

readout.source_of_truth: GA4 key event waitlist_signup, campaign smoke-studio-memberships; rows for other campaigns left out: retargeting-trial
checks: Every promise passed its planned 268 visits.
Land rates 0.81, 0.829, 0.811 sit within 20% of their average, so no page version lost visitors to a slow load or a broken link.
Meta counted 51 leads against 48 sign-ups in GA4. The GA4 count decides; Meta's own count can include view-through credit and repeat submits.
findings: B (no more chasing payments) is a go: 8.54% of 316 visitors signed up, above the 5.77% pass line, at $19.33 a sign-up against $30.00 allowed.
A (recurring revenue) is real but short: 4.7% clears its critical rate of 4.48% but not the pass line; each sign-up cost $37.67.
C (price first) is a stop: 2.41% is under its critical rate of 4.5%. Leading with the price doesn't sell it.
B beat C (p 0.001) but is not proven better than A (p 0.0564, needs under 0.025). The go rests on B clearing the line on its own, not on beating A.
readout.decision: Go on the test: lead the add-on with the late-payments promise, and keep recurring revenue as the second line on the page. Drop the price-first pitch.
readout.what_this_does_not_prove: Sign-ups are not purchases. The go uses the user's 20% sign-up-to-customer estimate; check it with a paid pre-order to the 48 sign-ups before building.
next: Email all 48 sign-ups the outcome by 2026-11-20, as the thank-you page promised.
If installed, idea-validation-plan makes the build call across this test and the pre-order.

not_checked: Reddit: no connector and no pasted costs.
